meta.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield, Long History (1871–Present)
meta.revision_note: FRED's H.15 monthly average (the 1953-04+ leg) is not revised after publication. The pre-1953 leg is a one-time historical compilation from Shiller/Yale's own long-term interest rate column; the site re-downloads his workbook on every fetch, so a correction there would appear on the next run, but none is expected.

inputs.label: Pre-1953 long-term interest rate (Shiller/Yale's "Rate GS10" column, 1871–1953)
10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate, monthly average (FRED GS10, 1953–present)

methodology: 1871-01 through 1953-03: Shiller/Yale's own long-term interest rate column ("Rate GS10" in ie_data.xls), read from the maintained shillerdata.com copy. Shiller's own documentation of how this column is built pre-1953 could not be located on his data pages or in the workbook itself (see catalog/sources/shiller.json); it is widely cited in finance literature as Sidney Homer's "A History of Interest Rates" spliced with the Treasury 10-year series from 1953 — consistent with, though not confirmed by, the exact value agreement at the seam (both legs read 2.83 for 1953-03/1953-04).
1953-04 onward: FRED's GS10, the monthly average of the daily H.15 constant-maturity 10-year yield — FRED's earliest published month for this series.

The two legs are compared at the seam on every fetch (fetch_gs10_long.py's check_seam) and a divergence beyond 0.10 percentage points is logged, not enforced, since Shiller could restate his historical column independently of FRED.
notes: Values are percent (4.25 means 4.25%), not a decimal fraction.

Every observation carries `source` ("shiller" or "fred") and `frequency` ("monthly") — the per-observation metadata pattern this chart establishes for future stitched series. site/js/charts/timeseries.js shows the source in each point's tooltip.

The Shiller input's `publication_lag_business_days` is nominal and `required` is false: 1871-01–1953-03 is a fixed historical range that never advances, so it never gates the dataset's overall `due_by` — only the FRED leg does.

Decided 2026-09-17 (user): this column has no S&P component, so it publishes even though the rest of Shiller's workbook (price, dividends, earnings, CAPE) stays local-only pending S&P's terms. See CLAUDE.md's Licence Notes and catalog/sources/shiller.json.
